title: Retype ChannelPermission.target_type from String to a typed enum (spec: 'role' | 'user')
description:
Found while resolving bd:JMAP-ly0n.3 (ChatPresenceEvent.presence). The bead explicitly flagged this as a parallel issue: ChannelPermission.target_type (crate-jmap-chat-types/src/chat.rs:59) is typed String, but the spec (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.15) enumerates 'role' | 'user'.

Fix: add a new typed enum (TargetType or ChannelPermissionTargetType) using impl_string_enum! with Role, User, and Other(String) for forward-compat. Same pattern as Presence, DeliveryState, ReadDisposition, ChatKind. Change target_type's type from String to the new enum.

Scope: src/chat.rs (one struct field + new enum), test additions for the typed dispatch + Other(_) forward-compat, README update if enum surface is documented there. Probably zero downstream consumer breakage — no current code matches on ChannelPermission.target_type as a typed string per the bd:JMAP-ly0n.3 investigation, but verify before committing.

Smaller consumer surface than .3 so lower priority, but same canonical-template hygiene rationale: workspace AGENTS.md anoints jmap-chat-types as canonical for the wire format and the spec enumerates the values.
notes: Folded into JMAP-y3f2 (Chat core server conformance (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00)) by the 2026-10-19 spec gap audit. Bead text says 'role' | 'user'; draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 L772 says 'role' | 'member'.
